metadata.title: Vemurafenib Monotherapy
metadata.indication: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Current source reconciled; independent clinical/pharmacy review pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: NCCP tables individually reconciled; proposed candidate awaits validation and independent clinical/pharmacy approval.

supplemental_source_documents.section: Current EMA product information supplement, component-specific

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or the specialist authority specified in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: All modifications require consultant/pharmacy review. Component-specific advice and dose levels are reference text, never an automatically calculated prescription. Missing values remain unassessed.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding derived from NCCP 00102 Version 6. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

source_conflicts.resolution: Exactly 60 ms change is not covered by the printed <60 and >60 rows. Withhold and seek consultant interpretation.

NCCP baseline ECG is worded for at-risk patients and skin visits week 8 then q12-weeks; current EMA requires ECG/electrolytes for all patients and monthly prescriber skin examinations. Preserve the fuller SmPC surveillance, distinguish specialist dermatology visits from routine prescriber skin review, and confirm the team plan.

removed_unsupported_generic_rules: Legacy shared whole-regimen QT/LVEF/CK/ILD/haemorrhage shortcuts were replaced only where a source-specific pathway exists. Named symptoms without source dose criteria prompt assessment, not invented thresholds.

indications.description: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.

treatment.schedule_summary: Vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily continuously; use a 28-day assessment-cycle convention. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
treatment.cycle_convention_note: 28 days is an assessment convention; treatment is continuous without planned breaks.

administration.note: Approximately 12 hours apart, continuously; 28 days is a review convention, not a planned break.

action.message: QTc >500 ms at baseline: vemurafenib treatment is not recommended.

rules.explanation: QTc >500 ms at baseline: vemurafenib treatment is not recommended.

action.message: QTc >500 ms requires interruption of vemurafenib and review of baseline change and prior occurrences. Correct reversible causes; resumption requires QTc strictly <500 ms.

rules.explanation: QTc >500 ms requires interruption of vemurafenib and review of baseline change and prior occurrences. Correct reversible causes; resumption requires QTc strictly <500 ms.

action.message: QTc >500 ms AND increase >60 ms from pretreatment: permanently discontinue vemurafenib.

rules.explanation: QTc >500 ms AND increase >60 ms from pretreatment: permanently discontinue vemurafenib.

action.message: An episode with QTc >500 ms and >60 ms increase requires permanent discontinuation even if the current QTc has recovered.

rules.explanation: An episode with QTc >500 ms and >60 ms increase requires permanent discontinuation even if the current QTc has recovered.

action.message: SOURCE BOUNDARY GAP: the NCCP table specifies >60 ms for permanent cessation and <60 ms for the interruption/reduction rows; exactly 60 ms is not allocated. Keep vemurafenib withheld and obtain specialist interpretation; do not automatically restart or invent a permanent-stop boundary.

rules.explanation: SOURCE BOUNDARY GAP: the NCCP table specifies >60 ms for permanent cessation and <60 ms for the interruption/reduction rows; exactly 60 ms is not allocated. Keep vemurafenib withheld and obtain specialist interpretation; do not automatically restart or invent a permanent-stop boundary.

action.message: Record the actual pretreatment QTc before classifying the >60 ms change; current QTc >500 ms still independently requires interruption.

rules.explanation: Record the actual pretreatment QTc before classifying the >60 ms change; current QTc >500 ms still independently requires interruption.

action.message: Record first, second or third QTc >500 ms occurrence; recurrence changes the reduction/permanent-stop pathway.

rules.explanation: Record first, second or third QTc >500 ms occurrence; recurrence changes the reduction/permanent-stop pathway.

action.message: First occurrence: interrupt until QTc <500 ms; reference restart is 720 mg twice daily, or 480 mg twice daily if already reduced. Consultant/pharmacy must verify the current dose.

rules.explanation: First occurrence: interrupt until QTc <500 ms; reference restart is 720 mg twice daily, or 480 mg twice daily if already reduced. Consultant/pharmacy must verify the current dose.

action.message: Second occurrence: interrupt until QTc <500 ms; reference restart is 480 mg twice daily, or permanent discontinuation if already at 480 mg twice daily. Consultant/pharmacy must verify the current dose.

rules.explanation: Second occurrence: interrupt until QTc <500 ms; reference restart is 480 mg twice daily, or permanent discontinuation if already at 480 mg twice daily. Consultant/pharmacy must verify the current dose.

action.message: Third QTc >500 ms occurrence requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation; later QT recovery does not remove the stop history.

rules.explanation: Third QTc >500 ms occurrence requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation; later QT recovery does not remove the stop history.

action.message: Second QT episode when vemurafenib is already reduced to 480 mg twice daily: permanently discontinue.

rules.explanation: Second QT episode when vemurafenib is already reduced to 480 mg twice daily: permanently discontinue.

action.message: Do not restart at QTc 500 ms: the source recovery threshold is strictly <500 ms.

rules.explanation: Do not restart at QTc 500 ms: the source recovery threshold is strictly <500 ms.

action.message: Severe vemurafenib hypersensitivity requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Severe vemurafenib hypersensitivity requires permanent discontinuation.

action.message: A severe dermatological reaction, including SJS/TEN/DRESS, requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation. This overrides the generic first-grade4 consultant-choice row.

action.message: Current EMA product information does not recommend vemurafenib with uncorrectable electrolyte abnormalities or long QT syndrome; reconcile before prescribing.

rules.explanation: Current EMA product information does not recommend vemurafenib with uncorrectable electrolyte abnormalities or long QT syndrome; reconcile before prescribing.

action.message: Other intolerable grade 2 or grade 3 toxicity: interrupt until grade 0–1. First event: reference restart 720 mg twice daily, or 480 mg if already reduced. Second event: 480 mg twice daily, or stop if already at 480 mg. Third event: permanently discontinue. Confirm recurrence/current dose.

rules.explanation: Other intolerable grade 2 or grade 3 toxicity: interrupt until grade 0–1. First event: reference restart 720 mg twice daily, or 480 mg if already reduced. Second event: 480 mg twice daily, or stop if already at 480 mg. Third event: permanently discontinue. Confirm recurrence/current dose.

action.message: Third occurrence/persistence after two reductions of intolerable grade 2/grade 3 toxicity requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Third occurrence/persistence after two reductions of intolerable grade 2/grade 3 toxicity requires permanent vemurafenib discontinuation.

action.message: The second intolerable grade 2/grade 3 event at an existing 480 mg twice-daily dose requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: The second intolerable grade 2/grade 3 event at an existing 480 mg twice-daily dose requires permanent discontinuation.

action.message: Grade 4 first occurrence: consultant chooses permanent discontinuation OR interruption until grade 0–1 with reference restart at 480 mg twice daily; stop if already at 480 mg. This is not an automatic restart decision.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 first occurrence: consultant chooses permanent discontinuation OR interruption until grade 0–1 with reference restart at 480 mg twice daily; stop if already at 480 mg. This is not an automatic restart decision.

action.message: Second grade 4 occurrence/persistence after first reduction requires permanent discontinuation; recovery cannot erase the episode history.

rules.explanation: Second grade 4 occurrence/persistence after first reduction requires permanent discontinuation; recovery cannot erase the episode history.

action.message: Grade 4 toxicity when vemurafenib is already 480 mg twice daily requires permanent discontinuation.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 toxicity when vemurafenib is already 480 mg twice daily requires permanent discontinuation.

action.message: A further reduction below 480 mg twice daily is not recommended; reconcile the permanent-stop or consultant-choice pathway.

rules.explanation: A further reduction below 480 mg twice daily is not recommended; reconcile the permanent-stop or consultant-choice pathway.

action.message: Concomitant other anticancer therapy is an exclusion for this monotherapy protocol; select and verify an appropriate combination protocol instead.

action.message: Current EMA requires a decision to discontinue breastfeeding or vemurafenib after weighing maternal treatment benefit and infant risk. Confirm the specialist plan before exposure; do not assume concurrent breastfeeding is safe.

eligibility: Adult unresectable/metastatic melanoma with validated BRAF V600 mutation
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
Regimen-specific exclusions encoded in the assessment

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Highest emetogenic active component and current NCCP classification.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
supportive_care.source_audit_note: Vemurafenib monotherapy: minimal emetogenic potential; dabrafenib and cobimetinib/vemurafenib: minimal-to-low. Premedication not usually required; antiemetics per local policy. No default prophylactic medicines prescribed.

baseline: ECG/QT evaluation for patients at risk
Dermatological evaluation for other skin cancer
Chest CT as part of metastatic melanoma staging
during: FBC, renal and liver profile before each 28-day assessment cycle
ECG every four weeks for the first twelve weeks, then every twelve weeks and after dose modification
Dermatology at week eight, then every twelve weeks by oncology/dermatology
If severe hepatic impairment: liver biochemistry twice weekly
after: Follow the individual oncology/dermatology plan; contraception for at least six months after treatment
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Consultant treatment plan; no universal response-imaging cadence or tumour-marker panel is specified.
smPC_supplement: EMA Zelboraf: ECG/electrolytes including magnesium in ALL patients before treatment, after one month and after dose modification (NCCP00102 baseline wording says at-risk only).
EMA Zelboraf: prescriber skin examination monthly during treatment and up to six months afterwards; reconcile with NCCP00102 week 8 then q12-week dermatology schedule.
EMA Zelboraf: head/neck baseline and every 3 months, chest CT baseline and every 6 months for secondary malignancy surveillance; anal/pelvic examination before/end treatment when indicated.
